fields.security_summary: AHCI 1.3.1 itself defines no cryptographic / authentication / confidentiality features. The base protocol provides only line-level data integrity via a 32-bit CRC on every FIS (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, defined by Serial ATA 2.6) plus framing primitives (SOF / EOF / R_OK / R_ERR). Higher-level security — Drive Lock / ATA Security Feature Set (passwords, secure-erase, freeze-lock), TCG Opal / Pyrite / Ruby (self-encrypting drives), Sanitize Device Feature Set — is layered on top via ATA commands sent through the standard AHCI Command List path, but those features are device-side. The AHCI BIOS/OS Handoff mechanism (CAP2.BOH + BOHC) prevents BIOS / OS ownership races, which has a security flavor but is not a confidentiality control.

security_features.name: FIS CRC-32 (Serial ATA 2.6)
security_features.scope: Every FIS payload (FIS Type byte through last data Dword)
security_features.description: Polynomial 0x04C11DB7; defeats wire-level bit-flip errors and most accidental corruption. NOT a cryptographic MAC.

security_features.name: 8b/10b encoding running-disparity detection
security_features.description: Detects most single-bit errors via running-disparity violations; reported via PxSERR.DIAG.DB (10b-decode error).

security_features.name: BIOS/OS Handoff (CAP2.BOH + BOHC)
security_features.scope: HBA controller ownership between BIOS / OS
security_features.description: BOHC.BOS / OOS / OOC / SOOE / BB fields coordinate which agent (BIOS firmware vs OS kernel) currently controls the HBA — prevents concurrent-issue races. Not a confidentiality / authentication control.

security_features.name: Command List Override (PxCMD.CLO)
security_features.description: When CAP.SCLO=1, software can force PxTFD.STS.BSY / DRQ clear without device cooperation — required for software-reset of an unresponsive device.

security_features.name: ATA Security Feature Set (device-side, ATA-7+)
security_features.description: Sent through CFIS as a normal ATA command: SECURITY SET PASSWORD / UNLOCK / ERASE PREPARE / ERASE UNIT / FREEZE LOCK / DISABLE PASSWORD. Optional, device-implemented; AHCI is just the transport.

security_features.name: TCG Opal / Pyrite / Ruby (device-side, TCG SSC)
security_features.description: Sent via ATA TRUSTED RECEIVE / TRUSTED SEND ACS-4 commands; AHCI transports the CFIS + data; encryption / key management is device-internal.

security_features.name: SANITIZE Feature Set (device-side, ACS-4)
security_features.description: SANITIZE BLOCK ERASE / CRYPTO SCRAMBLE / OVERWRITE — irreversible; reports progress via SANITIZE STATUS.

fields.no_base_layer_confidentiality: The AHCI / SATA base protocol does NOT encrypt user data on the wire. An attacker with physical bus access can capture plaintext blocks. Application-layer encryption (filesystem-level, dm-crypt / BitLocker, or hardware Self-Encrypting Drive via TCG Opal) is the recommended path for sensitive data.
fields.no_authentication_on_wire: AHCI / SATA do not authenticate the device or the host. A malicious replacement device cannot be distinguished from a legitimate one at the protocol level. Higher-level attestation (TCG SSC, vendor SMART, OS pairing) is required if device identity matters.
fields.comparison_to_sibling_nvme: NVMe / NVMHCI offer the same level of base-protocol security (CRC integrity only); NVMe extensions (Namespace Sanitize, Secure Erase, TCG Opal SSC) parallel the ATA / AHCI options. AHCI 1.3 included NVMHCI hooks (CAP2.NVMP) so the same silicon can host both protocols.
fields.notes: AHCI 1.3.1 itself documents no cryptographic mechanism. All confidentiality / authentication / integrity beyond the wire CRC and 8b/10b disparity detection is delegated to the attached device's ATA Security / TCG / Sanitize implementation. The host-bus side (PCI / PCIe) is also out of scope — IOMMU / SR-IOV / SVA security controls live at the PCIe Root Complex layer.
